cards.text: Psalm 111 opens with one word: "Hallelujah!" No warm-up, no clearing his throat, the writer comes in HOT. He's going to thank the LORD with all his heart, and he's already picked out the spot.

cards.question: The psalmist is ready to give thanks to the LORD with all his heart. Where's he going to do it?

answers.text: Among the upright in the assembly

cards.text: Then he gets to the why. The works of the LORD are great, and the folks who love those works don't just glance at them and keep scrolling.

cards.question: The great works of the LORD are ___ by all who delight in them.

cards.text: The psalmist calls God's work splendid and majestic. Me? My most majestic work ever was a cookie that came out perfectly round, and I STILL bring it up at parties.

cards.question: Right alongside God's splendid and majestic work, the psalmist mentions His righteousness. How long does it endure?

cards.text: Take it from a stamper who spent years in the back of a junk drawer: people FORGET things. But the LORD makes sure His wonders don't end up where I did.

cards.question: True or false: the psalmist says the LORD has kept His wonders hidden away.

cards.text: Then the psalmist tells you what the LORD is like: "the LORD is gracious and compassionate." And he shows you exactly what that looks like.

cards.question: The gracious and compassionate LORD looks after His people. He provides ___ for those who fear Him.
True or false: the psalmist says the LORD remembers His covenant forever.

cards.text: Then the psalmist brings receipts. Not a rumor, not a screenshot from somebody's group chat: God has SHOWN His people the power of His works.

cards.question: How did the LORD show His people the power of His works?

answers.text: By giving them the inheritance of the nations
By parting the sea right in front of them
By sending fire down on all their enemies

cards.text: The works of His hands are truth and justice. Then the psalmist moves from what God does to what God says: His precepts.

cards.question: A God whose works are truth and justice gives instructions you can lean on. All His precepts are ___.
True or false: the psalmist says the LORD's precepts hold for a while and then get replaced.

cards.text: They're upheld forever and ever, enacted in truth and uprightness. Meanwhile, the coupon I shared a junk drawer with expired YEARS ago, and it STILL believes in itself.
Then comes the big one. God did something for His people that you only need when you're stuck somewhere you can't get yourself out of, and believe me, I KNOW that feeling.

cards.question: The psalmist tells what the LORD did for His people: He has sent ___ to His people.
The psalmist says the LORD has ordained His covenant forever. Then he describes the LORD's name. What does he call it?

cards.text: Now the psalmist lands the plane. After all those great works and trustworthy precepts, he tells you where wisdom starts.

cards.question: According to the psalmist, what is the beginning of wisdom?
True or false: the psalmist says all who follow the LORD's precepts gain rich understanding.

cards.text: He opened with Hallelujah, and he closes with praise too: "His praise endures forever!" Me? I finish my songs by humming because I forgot the words.

findings.problem: This is a 'where' question, but the wrong answers 'Alone on a quiet hillside' and 'Inside the king's own palace' are generic settings, not real places or details from the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The joke says Papa Dorin 'STILL' brings up his cookie 'at parties.' He lives alone on the cookie planet, so going to parties adds something new to his world. It is not a small moment or habit around his bakery.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The card says 'And he shows you exactly what that looks like.' That claims verse 5 is the psalmist's illustration of verse 4's 'gracious and compassionate.' The text puts the two lines side by side but never says how they connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question begins 'The gracious and compassionate LORD looks after His people.' This links verse 4 to verse 5 as cause and example, which the text leaves open. It also says 'His people' where verse 5 says 'those who fear Him.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'By parting the sea right in front of them' is a real act of God's power for His people elsewhere in Scripture. Since the question doesn't say 'according to the psalmist,' a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The question's setup, 'gives instructions you can lean on,' already means 'trustworthy.' It rules out the wrong answers 'temporary' and 'hidden' and gives the answer away. It also adds a link between verse 7's two halves ('A God whose works are truth and justice gives...') that the text leaves open.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card uses its words to define 'redemption' ('something ... you only need when you're stuck somewhere you can't get yourself out of'), which turns the next card into a riddle. The definition also isn't in the text.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The question asks what words the psalmist uses for the LORD's name ('Holy and awesome' vs 'Hidden and secret' vs 'Gentle and quiet'). Nothing before it gives a reason to pick one. This is guessing the wording of a line, like the bad Psalm 23 example about what David's head is anointed with.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
